elements.element: Renewal requires mutual written agreement unless every conditional automatic-renewal element below is met.
elements.evidence: Renewal remains automatic ("Each Service Option Attachment will renew automatically..."), so the mutual-written-agreement route is not used; the conditional automatic-renewal elements below (12-month cap, 30-day opt-out, 60-day reminder) are not all satisfied, so this element fails.

elements.element: If renewal is automatic, each renewal term is no longer than 12 months.
elements.evidence: Retained language renews "for an additional term equal in duration to the previous term" — no 12-month ceiling; if an Order Form term exceeds 12 months this rolls into a multi-year renewal.

elements.element: If renewal is automatic, Customer may opt out on no more than 30 days' notice.
elements.evidence: Rendered clause requires notice "at least 60 days prior to the end of the then-current term" — meets fallback ceiling but exceeds the 30-day preferred opt-out.

elements.element: If renewal is automatic, Vendor must remind Customer at least 60 days before renewal.
elements.evidence: No reminder obligation appears anywhere in the rendered § 3.2 or the charges paragraph; the comment acknowledges the reminder is only a preferred position, not drafted.

elements.element: If renewal permits price increases, each increase is capped at the lesser of CPI and 3 percent.
elements.evidence: Condition does not apply: the renewal clause contains no uplift mechanic and § 4.1 fixes Charges as "specified in Service Option Attachments and Order Forms" with no renewal escalation right, so no price-increase permission exists to cap.

elements.element: If renewal is automatic, Customer's non-renewal notice window is no more than 60 days.
elements.evidence: Operative text now reads "unless either party notifies the other party in writing at least 60 days prior to the end of the then-current term" — a 60-day window, at the fallback ceiling. The deterministic check reporting "number not found" is a format artefact (the numeral is unaccompanied by a spelled-out word); substantively the 60-day figure is present.

elements.element: If renewal permits price increases, each increase is capped at 5 percent.
elements.evidence: Condition not triggered: Charges are set solely by the Service Option Attachments and Order Forms and no renewal-time uplift or indexation right is granted to IBM in the cited provisions.

reasons: Fallback is complete: the only operative change replaces "ninety (90) days" with "60 days", bringing the non-renewal notice window to the fallback ceiling; the conditional 5 percent uplift element is inapplicable because no renewal price-increase mechanic exists in the Agreement's charging provisions.

Preferred remains incomplete for three named defects the drafter would need to cure in operative language: (i) cap each renewal term at twelve (12) months rather than "a term equal in duration to the previous term"; (ii) reduce Customer's opt-out to thirty (30) days; (iii) insert an express IBM obligation to notify Customer of the upcoming renewal at least sixty (60) days before the end of the then-current term.

Minimality holds: no word outside the target element was deleted or paraphrased, the mutual structure, term-end anchoring, writing requirement and the charges paragraph are untouched, and no extras (survival tails, procedures, uplift formulas) were added.

Intent preserved: term-end timing, the per-Service Option Attachment structure, invoicing mechanics and all cross-references survive without contradiction or dangling terms. The symmetrical effect (IBM's own non-renewal notice also drops to 60 days) is an unavoidable consequence of the minimal edit to a mutual sentence, not an intent failure.

Escalation point correctly flagged rather than silently accepted: because the renewal term tracks the previous term, any Order Form term longer than 12 months converts this into an automatic multi-year renewal, which is walk-away territory under this rule and should be addressed at the Order Form level or by adding the 12-month cap.

Deterministic regex "non-renewal notice window ≤ 60 days: number not found" is a false negative on inspection — the rendered clause states "at least 60 days prior"; the check appears to expect the "sixty (60)" long form.
